Subject: Planned: CentralUS2 staged kernel-module (kmod) rollout — brief impact window

Hi Asha / CloudCart team,

Heads-up: we have scheduled a staged kernel-module (kmod) maintenance window for the CentralUS2 inference fleet where some of your workloads are currently running. This maintenance is targeted, low-risk work to deploy a fix for a socket-handling regression we surfaced in June.

Window (UTC): 2026-08-26 02:00 - 06:00 UTC (we will roll across zones to avoid any single-zone disruption).
Estimated customer impact: short, rolling instance restarts (typically ~30-90s per instance). For most requests you should see transient connection resets and a quick reconnect; streaming sessions may be interrupted and need to re-establish the websocket or stream. We expect no data loss for persisted KV caches; however active in-memory state will not survive a process restart.

Mitigations we will apply for this rollout:
- Staged per-AZ restarts with health checks and automatic rollbacks for any failed patch group.
- Preferred routing for critical pinned Dedicated capacity customers (reserved pools) to avoid restarts where possible.
- On-detection fallback to nearby region (WestUS) for traffic that can tolerate cross-region routing.

Attachments: centralus2-kmod-maintenance-summary.pdf (summary + timeline) and runbook-hotpatch-steps.txt (support steps & verification checklist).

Please let us know whether you have long-running streams or pinned sessions we should prioritize (reply with instance IDs or hubspot ticket reference). If we don't hear back, we will proceed as scheduled and open a support ticket to track any follow-up.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park

2) Are Dedicated / Reserved customers fully exempt from the restarts, or is there a maintenance path for reserved capacity as well? We have a subset of jobs on reserved instances.

Subject: Re: Planned: CentralUS2 staged kernel-module (kmod) rollout — brief impact window

Hi Asha — quick technical answers below.

1) Streaming sessions: the client SDK currently supports automatic reconnect, but it does not replay in-flight tokens. If your integration relies on reconstructed in-memory state, you should persist incremental checkpoints to your datastore or use the SDK's checkpoint API before the window. For the CC-RT-* flows, if you can provide example session IDs we can mark those instances for the first priority group to minimize restart probability.

2) Dedicated/reserved capacity: Reserved GPU pools that are pinned to your tenant will not be restarted as part of this staged patch unless you have opted into the maintenance window for those pools. From our inventory, CloudCart has a mix — two pinned pools (reserved) and three shared pools. The pinned pools will be excluded; the shared pools will see the kmod update. I can share the specific instance IDs in a follow-up message (or add them to the ticket).

3) Cross-region routing: there are no contract changes for temporary cross-region fallback during maintenance; we bill per usual usage. Latency and throughput differences apply — we recommend routing only for critical short-lived RPCs. Our runbook will attempt to maintain identical model variants when routing.

Mitigation suggestion: if you can mark critical streaming instance IDs now, we will place them into the no-restart group or schedule them early in the roll (minimizing the window).

Also: I have created a support ticket (CS-98721) to track CloudCart's impacted instances and runbook steps. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/CS-98721

Markus Klein
